scope_limits: No formal naming-registry verification; direct mapped reach labels remain bounded.

records.region: Castro Alves–Conceição do Almeida–Dom Macedo Costa–Muniz Ferreira–Nazaré–Jaguaripe corridor, Bahia, Brazil
records.geographic_disambiguation: Supported representative receiving-system identity for the researched composite, including its separately described estuarine margin. This is not a uniform hydronym for every headwater, tributary, estuarine branch or rendered terminal extension.
records.completion_scope: Bounded name and full-path source research complete for the sole stage 3 mainstem FID, all 21 stored parts, and both distinct endings. Only the supported representative candidate is proposed; accepted/scalar/Korean names remain null and all application flags false.
records.supported_name_scope: Supported representative receiving-system identity for the researched composite, including its separately described estuarine margin. This is not a uniform hydronym for every headwater, tributary, estuarine branch or rendered terminal extension.

scope_limits: The representative river identity does not authorize naming every selected small opening, tributary or estuarine patch Rio Jaguaripe. No distinct name is assigned to the chosen very first opening beyond its supported receiving-system connection.

The stored sea class is preserved as metadata. The source endpoint is within the estuary; the rendered endpoint is in its southern vegetated margin. The straight final rendered extension is not claimed to trace a mapped natural channel.
Historical generalized maps and mixed-age source compilations do not establish exact modern banks. The imagery scene date, tidal stage and present hydraulic conditions remain unknown.
Mapped tributaries Rio da Dona, Rio Aratuípe, Rio Onha and Rio Caboclo remain bounded names, not true aliases of the whole feature.
Formal registry status and Korean naming remain unverified. No product naming/application changes were made.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Separately named joining tributary in the Onha/Muniz Ferreira lower inland setting; not a whole-feature alias.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Western tributary entering the lower Jaguaripe near Aratuípe/Maragogipinho; not an alias or an appended selected reach.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio da Dona
bounded_name_observations.scope: Separately labelled southern estuarine river joining Jaguaripe east of the town peninsula. Its upper course is outside the selection and its name is not a Jaguaripe alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Caboclo
bounded_name_observations.scope: Separately labelled tidal creek south of the estuarine junction. Used only to describe the nearby rendered-ending margin; no claim that the straight rendered tail is its channel.

records.region: Northeastern Mexican interior; western intermontane valley and southeastern alluvial receiving floor
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: No supported representative natural-river name or true alias for this entire selected western valley/fan/plain composite. Regional Río Tula and other catchment names in authorial prose are not selected-route identities.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No supported representative natural-river name or true alias for this entire selected western valley/fan/plain composite. Regional Río Tula and other catchment names in authorial prose are not selected-route identities.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary geographic correspondence for all17 selected parts using three actually read photographic originals: northwestern opening, long southern valley, eastward foothill gap, central receiving-fan loop, southeast plain and actual alluvial-interior ending. No whole-selection hydronym is supported. This is a completed null name-scope hold, with no demonstrated missing basin-transfer link.
records.supported_name_scope: No supported representative natural-river name or true alias for this entire selected western valley/fan/plain composite. Regional Río Tula and other catchment names in authorial prose are not selected-route identities.

scope_limits: Photographic imagery supplies geographic correspondence, not hydronyms, registry decisions or exact current hydraulic continuity.
The valley/fan links are continuous ordinary receiving terrain. No currently wet thread through every field or dry patch is required or asserted.
Mosaic scene-date and color differences, localized haze and agricultural alteration limit fine-channel interpretation. No exact-bank, active gate/ditch operation or present water-state claim is made.
Regional basin and reach names from the2019 study are not assigned to this selection without a corresponding named map or adequate source-to-route prose.
The actual ending is an alluvial interior beside a broader drainage belt, not a proven named lake, sea mouth or observed subsurface continuation.
INEGI thematic map panels and SGM original mapping were not used; unresolved constituent relationships remain a source-use boundary, not a new access denial or a fabricated geographic transfer gap.

records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative receiving-system identity; not a scalar name for every tributary or upper fork.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete selected northern-tributary-to-Pacific route belongs to the Pisco receiving system. The seasonal Veladero drainage is a bounded tributary context; the exact first fork remains unnamed in this finding. No upper Chiris, Santuario or Huaytará main-course extension is assigned to this chosen opening.
records.completion_scope: Río Pisco is supported as the representative receiving system. All17 stored parts are geographically accounted for: the chosen eastern mountain feeder, broader seasonal northern tributary valley, direct join into Pisco, continuous middle/lower agricultural valley and Pacific outlet setting. The source sea endpoint and landward rendered coastal endpoint remain separately described. The upper tributary is not relabeled throughout as Pisco.
records.supported_name_scope: The complete selected northern-tributary-to-Pacific route belongs to the Pisco receiving system. The seasonal Veladero drainage is a bounded tributary context; the exact first fork remains unnamed in this finding. No upper Chiris, Santuario or Huaytará main-course extension is assigned to this chosen opening.

scope_limits: The exact name and upstream limit of the chosen easternmost feeder are unsupported. Veladero is retained as a bounded tributary context, while Pisco is the representative receiving-system identity.

Satellite mosaic epochs and contemporary water-management operations are unverified. The selected imagery shows no required lake/reservoir crossing or separate managed interbasin transfer; upstream reservoirs discussed by the report are outside the selected route.

Small clouds partly obscure local surface detail near lower part14; the common broad receiving valley and both continuations remain exposed at ordinary geographic scale. No current individual channel thread is inferred beneath cloud.

The final generalized segment is not a surveyed active channel. The source endpoint is offshore whereas the rendered endpoint is at the landward beach-margin outlet setting; neither is corrected or collapsed into the other.
Formal official-name registry verification has not been performed; accepted, whole-feature scalar and Korean names remain null and application remains disabled.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
